articleTitle: Fleet Intelligent Autonomous System for ART in Automated Container Terminals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: With the advancement of artificial intelligence and technologies, intelligent autonomous systems have been widely used in the logistics, transportation and maritim e industries. Intelligent autonomous systems can self-learn and adapt, and are capable of autonomous decision-making and operation in complex and dynamic environments, automatically adjusting and optimizing behaviors and functions by sensing the environment and users. The application of intelligent autonomous systems in Automated Container Terminals (ACT) has revolutionized the terminal and logistics industry. This paper introduces the application of the Fleet Intelligent Autonomous System (FIAS) in the ACT of Tianjin Port. The system mainly includes intelligent scheduling, dynamic path planning, intelligent traffic management, intelligent sequencing, intelligent charging scheduling, and intelligent parking management modules of the Artificial Intelligence Robot of Transportation (ART). The actual test data of the terminal shows that the proposed FIAS can effectively reduce the energy consumption of vehicle operation and improve the intelligent control level of the ART fleet.

articleTitle: Green Development Strategies for the Logistics Industry Based on “Carbon Peak and Carbon Neutral” Goals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: In the context of “Carbon Peak and Carbon Neutral”, the logistics industry faces enormous pressure for green development. This article analyzes the necessity of achieving the “Carbon Peak and Carbon Neutral” goals, the challenges faced by the green development of China's logistics industry, and issues less covered in research. It puts forward targeted strategic suggestions from both the government and enterprises. By strengthening green packaging, optimizing transportation routes, improving warehousing efficiency, and promoting clean energy, carbon emissions in the logistics industry can be effectively reduced, and sustainable development can be achieved. At the same time, the government and enterprises should work together to formulate complete regulations and standards, increase investment in research and development, cultivate professional talents, and provide strong support for the green development of the logistics industry.

articleTitle: Natural Language Processing and Sustainable Procurement Analysis of Procurement Data from Various Provinces
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: Logistics and procurement are both important components of the supply chain. Sustainable procurement is not only an important strategy for enterprises to pursue sustainable development, but also a key strategy for us to address environmental and social challenges. This study analyzed purchase order data from 31 provinces in China and evaluated and ranked them using the concept of sustainable procurement. Further utilize natural language processing and visualization techniques to classify texts and visualize them. This has reference significance for the analysis methods of sustainable procurement in the future.

articleTitle: Visual Measurement of Foam Thickness in Flotation Process Based on Depth Stereo Matching
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: In the process of copper flotation, the traditional detection method has some defects in accurately detecting the depth of foam layer in the flotation cell, especially for the identification of foam information of highly reflective and attenuation materials in the flotation foam system. We aim to introduce a new synthetic dataset, specifically for the flotation foam system, and pay special attention to the foam information of high reflection and high attenuation materials, so as to promote it to the actual flotation foam system and improve the accuracy of liquid level detection. We combine the newly synthesized dataset with binocular ranging methods and propose a soft strategy method for depth estimation of flotation cell thickness using binocular stereo matching based on IoT technology. The experimental results show that our method has achieved remarkable results in the flotation foam system, can accurately measure the depth of the flotation cell, and provides reliable technical support for the control and optimization of the flotation process. Therefore, this binocular stereo matching depth estimation method based on IoT technology provides an effective way to solve the limitations of traditional flotation depth detection methods. It not only effectively monitors the current efficiency of the flotation cell but also automatically identifies instances of flotation cell froth overflowing, offering automated inspection and diagnostics.

articleTitle: Research on Ship Fuel Consumption Prediction Based on LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: This article proposes a study on fuel consumption modeling and prediction based on data obtained from actual navigation monitoring of inland vessels, utilizing LSTM neural networks for modeling. The method selects 12 fuel consumption-related parameters, including main engine power and torque. Through analyzing the correlation and importance of the ship's fuel consumption characteristics, the significance of each factor's impact on fuel consumption is determined, verifying the interpretability and accuracy of the model. Finally, by comparing evaluation metrics with four other algorithms SVM, RFG, XGB, and GTB it was found that the LSTM model reduces the MSE by an average of 43.2%, MAE by 27.9%, and MAPE by 76.8%. This indicates that the LSTM neural network model has higher predictive accuracy, interpretability, and generalization ability compared to other prediction models, achieving a more precise fit to the target data.

articleTitle: Predictions of Low-carbon Travel Mode Choices for Residents Based on Stacking Ensemble Learning Prediction Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: The choice of low-carbon travel modes by residents directly affects the low-carbon development of transportation. Whereas, the current study of behavior prediction models lacks the accuracy and interpretability. We propose the theoretical framework of residents' low-carbon travel choice behavior at the microlevel and construct the Stacking ensemble learning prediction model on basis of residents' low carbon travel data. Through integrating various data such as transportation facility data and real-time weather observation data, we utilize machine learning algorithms to improve the prediction accuracy of residents' low-carbon travel choice, and explore the impact of different influencing factors on their choice behaviors.

articleTitle: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for Capacitated Facility Location Problems with Discrete Expansion Sizes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: Capacitated facility location problem (CFLP) is a classical combinatorial optimization problem widely applied in the domains of distribution, transportation planning, and telecommunication. As a typical NP-hard optimization problem, CFLPs featured by combinatorially high-dimensional decision spaces are not easily solved by most conventional methods. To appropriately handle the hard nature of CFLPs, we propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based framework to address CFLPs with discrete expansion sizes. Since a solution to the investigated CFLP can be sequentially constructed by partial solutions, we reformulated the CFLP as a Markov decision process with an unfixed and discrete time horizon. A deep Q-network (DQN)-based framework is adopted to learn the policy parameters and location solution. We experimentally demonstrate that our proposed approach can effectively find near-optimal solutions for CFLPs.

articleTitle: Probing an Augmented Reality-Assisted Human-Robot Collaborative Assembly Approach Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: In order to address the issue of insufficient attention to human factors in existing research on task allocation and sequence planning for human-robot collaborative assembly, a multi-dimensional and multi-scale representation method for human-robot collaborative assembly tasks is proposed. The method involves multiple aspects such as the difficulty of human-robot picking up transportation components. A solution model based on the improved Multi Agent Advantage Actor Critic algorithm is proposed to address the difficulties in task allocation and sequence planning solutions for human-robot collaborative assembly of complex products. Experimental results show that the proposed method can improve the efficiency of human-robot collaborative assembly and improves personnel work conditions. Finally, a human-robot collaborative assembly assistance system is developed based on augmented reality technology, and the practical feasibility of the proposed method was verified.

articleTitle: Process Industry System Modeling Based on Time Series Imputation: A Case Study of Paste Thickener
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: In process CPS systems, highly accurate modeling of the production system is essential for optimal control, fault diagnosis, and flexible manufacturing. Traditional data-driven modeling of industrial processes focuses on predicting future trends based on variable periodicity and trends, often neglecting the impact of control variables. This paper proposes a new approach to improve CPS accuracy, particularly for systems heavily influenced by controlled variables. Firstly, CPS modeling is redefined as a time series imputation problem, introducing exogenous variables via a sequence modeling algorithm based on a state space model to enhance forecasting accuracy. Secondly, sequence inputs are encoded in patches, improving the model's ability to process local sequence information. The proposed method is evaluated on a real deep cone thickener underflow concentration forecasting task and compared with state-of-the-art time series forecasting methods, demonstrating superior performance. This study not only provides a more accurate model for CPS but also offers a framework for integrating control variables into predictive modeling.

articleTitle: Human-Intention Prediction with Visual-Language Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: Human-intention prediction is an important part of human-machine interaction wildly utilized in industrial intelligent systems. In recent years, large language models have expanded to the image task with outstanding performance, leading to an increasing attraction to the application of multimodal Large Language Models. However, the exploration of visual-language models in human-intention prediction is still limited. To address this gap, this paper investigates the effectiveness of visual-language models in predicting human intentions and successfully transfers the knowledge in LLMs to downstream classification tasks. Finally, this paper takes traffic scenarios as an example to validate the feasibility of the video-LLaMA model in predicting pedestrian behavior intentions.

articleTitle: The Role of Industry 4.0 and Digitalization in Bolstering Supply Chain Resilience: Evidence from the Hotel Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: The new global reality that has emerged from the COVID-19 pandemic has called for more resilient supply chains. Industry 4.0 technology (I4T) helps businesses achieve better performance. But the effects of I4T on service supply chain resilience are not clear. The purpose of this paper is to understand how I4T affects hotel supply chain resilience in the presence of the COVID-19 pandemic.

articleTitle: A Joint Strategy Study of Preventive Maintenance and Two-Dimensional Extended Warranty Coverage
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: The cost relationship between preventive maintenance and extended warranty often leads to conflicts of interest between manufacturers and consumers, and providing high-quality after-sales service that meets consumer interests has increasingly become an important cornerstone for manufacturers' survival. In view of this, this study aims to jointly optimize preventive maintenance strategies and extended warranty scope to reconcile such conflicts of interest. Firstly, We have established a two-dimensional warranty cost model and a consumer extended warranty utility model that takes into account the timing of consumers purchasing extended warranty services. Then, from the perspective of both manufacturers and consumers, a joint optimization model of preventive maintenance strategies and two-dimensional extended warranty periods is built. This model aims to determine the optimal extended warranty coverage and preventive maintenance strategies in different situations. Finally, taking a certain brand of automobile as an example, a numerical analysis of the main parameters in the model is conducted. This study provides theoretical support in assisting manufacturers to provide optimized two-dimensional extended warranty services that meet the interests of both parties.

articleTitle: Integrated Optimization on Tugboat Scheduling and Berth Allocation of Seaside Port Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: The current inefficiency in seaside operations at the port terminal has led to excessive waiting times for ships and environmental pollution. Traditional decision-making methods for berth allocation and tug scheduling plans have resulted in inefficiencies in the overall integrated process. In this study, a new mixed-integer linear programming model for optimizing tugboat scheduling and berth allocation at seaside port terminals is presented, aiming to minimize the weighted total stay time of ships while addressing the complexities of tugboat matching constraints, ship shift movements, and the heterogeneity of berths. Through computational experiments utilizing both practical port data and randomly generated instances, the model demonstrates significant improvements in operational efficiency and environmental impact reduction compared to traditional port scheduling methods. By focusing on the optimization of resource allocation and scheduling, the proposed model offers a comprehensive solution to the current inefficiencies faced by port terminals, highlighting its potential for practical implementation and its contribution towards more sustainable and effective port operations.

articleTitle: Knowledge-guided DRL for Resource Scheduling in Customized and Personalized Production
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: The manufacturing landscape has witnessed a paradigm shift towards multi-variety and small-batch production for the customized and personalized product (CPP). But this paradigm poses significant challenges for the cloud manufacturing system: 1) wired production machines cannot support the ultra-flexible resource allocation for the CPP job; 2) the scheduling model largely neglects the reconfiguration time of machines; 3) the intelligent scheduling method is difficult to learn the policy in the high-dimensional CPP solution space. To address these issues, we propose an edge-computing and wireless-connection based CPP manufacturing system framework which allows for the dynamic and ultra-flexible allocation of operations and resources. Then reconfiguration time is modelled in the optimization problem and a knowledge-guided deep reinforcement learning algorithm is proposed to effectively explore optimal CPP scheduling policy in the high dimensional solution space. The experimental results demonstrated that the proposed algorithm obtained better scheduling results than traditional scheduling rules, effectively balancing processing time and reconfiguration time, thereby minimizing the overall jobshop makespan.

articleTitle: Ripnet: Real-Time Obstacle Detection for USVs Based on Improved PSPNet
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: This paper introduces a real-time obstacle detection approach for USVs Based on Improved PSPNet (RipNet), a new semantic segmentation method with excellent detection accuracy and high frames-per-second (fps) performance. The proposed RipNet relies only on monocular visual input and has a lightweight structure, which makes RipN et easy to deploy on USVs. The improved structure of RipNet based on PSPNet (IPSPNet) expands the semantic information of coordinate di-rection, which further strengthens the semantic feature extraction and fusion. This improvement comes from the innovation module named Lightweight Coordinate Attention (LCA). Using the oceanographic dataset MaSTr1325 as the training set and MODD2 as the validation set, the results show that higher performance (94.2% F -score) is achieved respected to the latest state-of-the-art methods, while keeping faster inference (67fps on an NVIDIA GTX 2080Ti), which proves the effectiveness of the proposed semantic segmentation algorithm RipN et.

articleTitle: Computer-Vision-Based Non-Contact Paste Concentration Measurement*
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: For monitoring the paste concentration, existing techniques, such as ultrasonic concentration meters and neutron meters, suffer from radiation hazards and low precision in high concentrations. This paper proposes a novel non-contact concentration measurement method based on deep learning. With the dataset collected by preparing the paste with different concentrations and taking photographs from the paste surface, a convolutional neural network is trained to extract the features from images and predict the concentration. The experiments indicate that the measurement accuracy is close to 88.79 % for the manual stirring paste dataset and 91.42 % for the automatic stirring paste dataset, which are sufficient in industrial applications. As a substitution of traditional concentration measurement instruments, the proposed vision-based concentration measurement method is non-contact and its accuracy is sufficient in industrial applications.

articleTitle: AiFashion: Multi-Modal and Multi-Dimensional Large Model Based on Self-Trained Customer Digital-Twin for Fashion Design and Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: This paper presents the concept design and tech-nical roadmap of a novel AI -driven fashion design and clothing manufacturing platform, called AiFashion. The vision of AiFashion is enabling every customer to wear personalized and customized clothes at low costs and with shorter waiting times. By integrating advanced information techniques such as Digital Twins, Generative AI, and Large Language Models. AiFashion can revolutionize the entire lifecycle of fashion designing and clothing manufacturing. Compared with existing AI -assisted fashion tools, AiFashion is characterized by its self-training nature, customization, interactivity, and lifecycle orientation in the garment industry. The first module of AiFashion, Chat Customer, effectively captures multi-modal customer profiles, including shallow body parameters and underlying preferences. The second module, Chat Tailor is a fashion designer based on Generative AI, which automatically generates the most suitable clothes satisfying multi-dimensional demands such as occasion, weather, and budget. To efficiently produce customized and highly distinctive clothing designed by Chat Tailor in clothing factories, the third module, Chat Manufacturing, leverages its absorbed professional knowledge in task planning and resource scheduling by chatting with managers, supervisors, and operators in factories. This paper gives brief implementation plans for each module in AiFashion.

articleTitle: Research on the Evaluation Model of New Quality Productive Forces in Enterprises
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: A productivity evaluation index system for enterprises is constructed, which distinguishes 4 primary indicators, 11 secondary indicators, and several tertiary indicators. The weights are determined using the Analytic Hierarchy Process. At the same time, based on the self-learning and generalization performance of neural networks, the weights are dynamically adjusted according to the actual situation through training with a large amount of information data. The final evaluation score of the new quality productive forces for enterprises is obtained by inputting it into the hierarchical structure model.

articleTitle: Requirement Analysis of Prognostic Technique for Advanced Small Modular Reactor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: The Advanced Small Modular Reactor has the characteristics of high energy density and long-term stable operation. It can be used as an energy supply device to supply power for mines, islands and scientific research located in remote/closed areas. The main deployment scenario of small module reactor is remote areas with weak infrastructure such as transportation, water source and power supply, which puts forward high requirements for the safety, reliability, flexibility, robustness, rapid deployment and “unattended” capability of reactor operation. Therefore, it is urgent to study the intelligent operation and maintenance system of small module reactor that can realize the ability of “unattended monitoring”. And the Prognostic Technique is one of the parts. Firstly, this paper analyzes the functional requirements of the predictive technology of advanced small reactors. Then, the current status of predictive technology at home and abroad is reviewed.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis for a Wideband Bistable Energy Harvester with Effects of Magnetic Coupling and Barrier Decreasing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: A new nonlinear energy harvester with effects of magnetic coupling and barrier decreasing is presented and investigated in this article. The characteristics of co-bistability and variable barrier are skillfully realized by a pair of orthogonal spring oscillators facing a piezoelectric cantilever beam. The three-degree-of-freedom design makes its overall structure and operating principle more complex. An elaborate mathematical model is established according to the theories of Euler-Bernoulli beam, linear piezoelectricity, and single-point magnetic dipole. Numerical results show that the novel harvester has the advantages of both a bistable structure with variable potential saddle and a multi-modal system with multiple natural frequencies, namely, the low barrier and the 2nd resonance facilitate the formation of a wide range of effective frequency band. Specifically, the working bandwidth of the designed harvester can be theoretically increased by up to 165% (23.3 Hz vs. 8.8 Hz) compared to a traditional magnetically coupled nonlinear energy harvester. The experimental findings are qualitatively coincident with the simulation outcomes, which validates the broadband superiority of the developed harvester. Besides, it is also proved by stochastic vibration tests that the proposed harvester has a greater probability of surmounting the potential barrier to trigger energetic interwell oscillation in low-level ambient vibrations.

articleTitle: Benders Decomposition for Order Batching and Scheduling Consider Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: Under the trend of mass customization, customer orders show the characteristics of “multi-variety, small batch”, which has a great impact on the scheduling process of batch production enterprises with mass production. This paper studies the problem of order group and batch scheduling with equipment constraints, that is, the order group and batch scheduling that makes the total production cost lowest is found under the equipment and delivery time constraints. Especially, the processing time of different batch equipment is different and uncertain. Firstly, a mixed integer linear programming model is established for order group and batch scheduling problems with equipment constraints. Secondly, in order to realize the optimal decision of the model efficiently, the Benders decomposition is adopted to decompose the original model into the order group master problem and the batch scheduling problem of equipment with different capacities. In view of the uncertain parameters in the model, robust optimization is adopted to transform the uncertainty constraints into robust counterpart. For the convergence problem of decomposed model, the improved Benders cut is added to speed up the convergence. Finally, through numerical experiments, the effectiveness of the algorithm is tested, and its competitiveness is verified in solving the optimal solution of medium-sized or even larger problem cases.

articleTitle: Requirement Analysis of Monitoring Center for Intelligent Operation and Maintenance System of Small Modular Reactor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: The small module reactor has the characteristics of high energy density and long-term stable operation. It can be used as an energy supply device to supply power for mines, islands and scientific research located in remote/closed areas. The main deployment scenario of small module reactor is remote areas with weak infrastructure such as transportation, water source and power supply, which puts forward high requirements for the safety, reliability, flexibility, robustness, rapid deployment and “unattended” capability of reactor operation. Therefore, it is urgent to study the intelligent operation and maintenance system of small module reactor that can realize the ability of “unattended monitoring”. And the monitoring center is one of the parts. This paper analyzes the application scenarios of the “intelligent operation and maintenance system” for small modular reactors, clarifying the requirements for the monitoring center application scenarios, communication and monitoring methods, and functional requirementsfor small modular reactors.

articleTitle: Graph-Augmented Text-Based Floorplan Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: In the context of floorplan generation, a recent trend has emerged towards incorporating user-provided descriptive texts to deliver a more flexible and user-centric interface, en-abling direct user engagement in the design and configuration processes. However, extracting accurate information from text input to characterize corresponding floorplans is challenging due to the latent representation of semantic, geometric, and topological design details. Conversely, graph-based generation methods, while lacking geometric information, exhibit superior performance owing to the intuitive representation of spatial data in graph structures. Building upon this understanding, this paper proposes a dual-stage framework that augments text input with serialized graphs to leverage the complementary strengths of both modalities. The pre-training stage uses script-generated texts to empower a graph generator for producing corresponding graphs from descriptive texts and familiarize a floorplan generator with concatenated text and graph input. During the fine-tuning stage, the pre-trained graph generator, alongside an alternative graph generator based on prompt-driven large language models, is employed to provide augmented graphical knowledge for the floorplan generator based on manually annotated descriptive texts. Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments demon-strate the effectiveness of the proposed approach over the vanilla text- based floorplan generation method.

articleTitle: Rolling Horizon Cooperative Scheduling for the Transportation-Energy Coupling Network in Automated Container Ports
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: With the intelligent upgrading of automated ports and the electrification of port equipment, the continuous strengthening of the coupling degree of transportation-energy networks, the fluctuating operation demand and the uncertain energy structure present higher requirements for the cooperative operation management and energy efficiency improvement in the transportation-energy coupling network of automated ports. In this paper, considering the influence of uncertain factors such as port wind and solar production capacity, as well as market electricity prices, on port energy system, a rolling horizon cooperative scheduling method for the transportation-energy coupling network of automated container ports is proposed. Firstly, by analyzing the port container operation process and the topology of the port energy network, the transportation-energy coupling relationship and the potential for energy conservation and emission reduction are explored. A three-stage cooperative rolling scheduling architecture comprising day-ahead, intra-day and real-time scheduling is then constructed. Subsequently, the day-ahead integer programming model and the intraday multi-commodity flow model are established respectively to realize cooperative scheduling optimization for the multi-scale automated port transportation-energy coupling network. Finally, based on the fluctuation information of wind and solar energy, real-time scheduling adjustments are implemented. According to the port operation rules, two heuristic scheduling strategies are summarized: the energy compensation strategy and task delay strategy. These strategies enable real-time feedback and facilitate flexible adjustments of port energy consumption structure to accommodate dynamic energy fluctuations. Experimental results demonstrate that the method can enhance the energy efficiency and energy structure stability of the port system, effectively improving energy conservation and emission reduction efficiency in the port, and promoting green and intelligent port construction.

articleTitle: A Driving Risk Field Model Considering Truck Performance and Levels of Automation for Automated Trucks in Ports
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: The driving risk field is an effective method for advancing autonomous driving decision control and risk warning. The existing risk field models primarily focus on urban roads and cannot be directly applied to ports. Therefore, based on the field theory, a unified driving risk field model for automated trucks has been proposed in this paper, which includes a kinetic field, a performance field, and an environment field. The performance factors of the automated truck, like the level of automation and the performance of systems, are critically incorporated into the model. This allows the model to accurately reflect the inherent risks of the automated truck during overloaded and excessive usage, thereby ensuring its operation safety. Two typical port scenarios are established to evaluate the performance of the proposed method. Simulation results demonstrate its excellent ability to reflect driving safety at ports. Through the variation in factor parameters, it is possible to discern the impact of each factor on the risk field. The final presentation meets the requirements of risk warning and provides a foundation for decision-making and route planning.

articleTitle: An Improved Diffusion Modeling Method with Environmental Priors for Robot Path Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: The path planning algorithms for robots have consistently been a central focus in related research domains. In recent years, with the increasing complexity of industrial environments and the demand for enhanced production efficiency, higher requirements have been placed on the planning efficiency and adaptability of robots. However, traditional planning methods based on discrete point sampling suffer from low planning efficiency and insufficient adaptability to complex scenarios. To address these issues, this paper proposes an improved path planning framework based on the diffusion model. The denoising process is utilized to sample paths from the posterior path distribution constrained by the obstacle environment. This framework employs the Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM) as the generative model and introduces a multi-head self-attention mechanism to better learn the feature representation between obstacles and viable paths. To reduce sampling time in DDPM, a skip-layer sampling method is introduced. Experiments under various environments are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Commuting Customized Bus Network Design Considering Price-Elastic Demand
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: As an important part of urban public transportation, customized bus fare system and route network are crucial to improving service quality and benign operation. In this work, we address a new commuting customized bus network design problem considering price-elastic demand. It aims to design a reasonable fare system and efficient route network. The objective is to maximize the total operating profit of considering penalty cost. We first formulate the problem as a mixed-integer programming (MIP) model. We simultaneously optimize customized bus routes, fares, travel time and passenger allocation. Based on problem properties, we develop an improved large neighborhood search algorithm (ILNS) to effectively solve the proposed model. Considering penalty cost, a greedy insertion operator calculating penalty cost during insertion process is designed to improve the algorithm's efficiency. Finally, computational results for a real case demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed model and algorithm.

articleTitle: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning-Based Real-Time Cooking Task Scheduling Optimization for Multi-Chef Collaborative Cooking
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: Nowadays, with the increasing living standard of people, there is a growing demand for the catering industry. Cooking efficiency is an important factor for restaurants to be highly competitive, and the efficient scheduling of cooking tasks of chefs matters the most. To enable efficient multi-chef collaborative cooking for restaurants, in this paper, a novel real-time cooking task scheduling method, MAPPO-LSTM, is proposed. In the MAPPO-LSTM, firstly, the proximal policy optimization (PPO) algorithm is augmented with a centralized training and distributed execution scheme to address the modeling of cooking task allocation for multiple chefs. Besides, convolutional neural networks (CNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM) are introduced to the actor network to mine temporal features of the cooking environment and to enhance the memory of historical cooking behavior sequences, respectively. Experiments are conducted using the “Overcooked” video game as the simulation environment. Compared with benchmarking methods, the high efficiency of the proposed MAPPO-LSTM for the real-time task scheduling in collaborative cooking is validated based on four indicators.

articleTitle: Driver and Pedestrian Acceptance of Highly Automated Vehicles: A TPB and UTAUT-Based Questionnaire Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: Highly automated vehicles (HAVs) can provide a safer and more efficient mobility, and the acceptance of automated driving in the general public is critical to the large-scale implementation of HAVs. Many studies have investigated car users' acceptance of HAVs, but only a few studies have considered the pedestrian's perspective. To fill the gap, four scales from Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and one scale from the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) were combined to construct the questionnaire survey from the perspectives of car users and pedestrians respectively. A totally of 629 participants joined the investigation. Mann-Whitney U test, correlation analysis and structural equation model was used to examine the relationship between the factors from TPB and UTAUT. The results indicate that that the acceptance of HAVs between pedestrians and car users was similar. Both car users' and pedestrians' intentions for HAVs were positively correlated to attitudes (including performance expectations), subjective norms, and perceived behavior control (PBC). We found that subjective norms and PBC were significant in influencing drivers to use HAV s. For pedestrians, attitudes, subjective norms and PBC were influenced on intentions. The results of the research can serve as a good reference for government agencies and companies to improve public acceptance and willingness to use HAVs.

articleTitle: Blockchain Technology for Logistics Collaboration in Physical Internet
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: This paper examines the potential contribution of blockchain (BC) technology to the Physical Internet (PI) for enhancing logistics collaboration management, and proposes a forward-looking deployment framework. Inspired by the digital internet, PI is a worldwide emerging logistics paradigm that advocates the interconnection of independent and heterogeneous logistics networks for the mutual sharing of services and assets. Such a paradigm will fundamentally challenge current operations management models and practices to achieve PI-based cooperation and co-opetition. New information technologies, notably BC technology including smart contracts and tokens, are considered promising in this regard. This paper aims to contribute to research by investigating why and how BC can be used in PI from the perspective of collaboration management. We then propose a framework for the deployment of BC in PI from operational to strategic levels. The key requirements as well as challenges to applying state-of-the-art BC technology to PI are also investigated.

articleTitle: Dynamic Berthing and Crane Allocation Considering Heterogeneous Vessels Under Tidal Influence
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: In port operations, tidal influence and heterogeneous vessels significantly affect berthing time and positions. In this work, we address a new dynamic berthing and crane allocation problem considering heterogeneous vessels under tidal influence. It aims to desgn a reasonable berth planning quay crane allocation system. The objective is to minimize the the vessels' total berthing costs, which includes the deviation costs, the waiting and delay costs. We first formulate the problem into a mixed-integer linear programming model. We simultaneously optimize the berthing and departure times, berth positions, and quay crane assignments. Using actual berthing data from Fuzhou Jiangyin port, our model identifies the most effective berthing solution for 10 vessels solved by CPLEX. Finally, computational results for a real case demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed model.

Author Keywords: Berth allocation and quay cranes assignment

articleTitle: Improving Intent Recognition with Multimodal Supervision for Human-Robot Interaction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: Human-Robot Collaborative Assembly enhances ef-ficiency by enabling robots to work alongside human operators in shared tasks. Accurately understanding human intent is essential for achieving high levels of collaboration, yet it remains a challenge, especially in industrial settings. To improve the proactive cognitive abilities of robots, this study introduces a novel approach that uses labeled text as semantic supervision within a multi-modal framework to address the video-text matching problem. Furthermore, the employment of pre-trained weights from large models leads to superior performance in downstream tasks. Comparative and ablation studies conducted on various industry-like datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves optimal benchmarks.

articleTitle: Quality Inspection Data-Driven Sampling Strategy and Path Optimization of Coordinate Measuring Machines for Body-in-White
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: The detection of shape accuracy of body-in-white (BIW) via coordinate measuring machines (CMM) is a critical process in automobile manufacturing quality management. Traditional CMM inspection for a whole BIW requires an exhaustive examination of over 2000 measuring points and takes up to eight hours. To improve the inspection efficiency, in this paper, a novel sampling strategy and detection path optimization method that leverages historical quality inspection data instead of computer-aided design (CAD) models is proposed. In the proposed method, three key attributes of measuring points are first defined based on quality data, and a sampling point optimization model is established. Next, genetic algorithm (GA) is used to determine the most efficient and effective sampling point subsets for reducing the number of measuring points. Based on the selected points, the detection path planning problem is then formulated as a traveling salesman problem (TSP) and solved via particle swarm optimization (PSO). Based on a real dataset, the proposed method is proved effective in reducing the number of sampling points while preserving the integrity of defect detections.

articleTitle: Rolling Bearing Fault Diagnosis Based on Improved Multi-Scale Dispersion Entropy and Deep Extreme Learning Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: In response to the challenges associated with the incomplete extraction of fault features in rolling bearings and the resultant low recognition accuracy, this study proposes a fault diagnosis model that integrates local mean decomposition, enhanced multi-scale dispersion entropy, and a whale optimization algorithm to refine the deep extreme learning machine. Initially, the model employs local mean decomposition to break down the original vibration signal into several product function components. Subsequently, spurious product function signal components are eliminated through the application of mutual information and kurtosis screening criteria. The multi-scale fault features of the signal components are then extracted using the improved multi-scale dispersion entropy method. Finally, the extracted fault features are fed into a deep extreme learning machine, which has been optimized via the whale optimization algorithm, for training and testing purposes. Experimental investigations conducted on rolling bearings, alongside comparisons with a control group, demonstrate that the proposed model effectively extracts fault features and enhances the identification accuracy of rolling bearing faults.

articleTitle: Enhance the Efficiency and Safety of Intelligent Coal Transportation Ports with AI and Big Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: This research addresses the challenges of large data volume, low utilization efficiency, and insufficient analysis and processing in the study and practice of intelligent ports. Focusing on a port for coal transportation, the study employs artificial intelligence processing algorithms as its core. It leverages existing advanced equipment and management systems to enhance the value of big data. The research establishes a framework for distributed data collection, heuristic production scheduling, and efficient anomaly detection. Based on this technology, the system achieves the goal of comprehensively and accurately reflecting the port's operational situation, avoiding the safety hazards of spontaneous coal combustion and significantly improving operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Ship Traffic Flow Prediction Using EEMD-edRVFL-RF
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: To predict the flow of ships arriving at anchorage., this paper proposes an advanced prediction framework named as EEMD-edRVFL-RF., which integrates the ensemble empirical mode decomposition (EEMD) method with ensemble deep random vector functional link network using random forest (edRVFL-RF) model. The subsequences decomposed from EEMD and original data are input into the edRVFL-RF model for prediction. In the EEMD-edRVFL-RF., a moving window strategy-based EEMD method is firstly utilized to decompose the original ship traffic flow sequence, which helps to reduce the data complexity and avoid data leakage. Then., K-fold cross-validation and grid search algorithm are introduced to determine the hyperparameters of the deep random vector functional connection network layer by layer. Afterwards, a RF model is inserted to define optimal weight of each output layer prediction in the network structure. Finally, the validity of the proposed framework is verified by using ship flow data of anchor at Three Gorges-Gezhou Dams Hub. The results demonstrate that the accuracy of the proposed framework is better than other classical ship flow prediction models. The prediction results can provide data support for Three Gorges-Gezhou Dams navigation authority to manage ship navigation.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Based Verifiable Decentralized Identities for Cyber-Physical Web 3.0
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: The Internet environment and activities with large volume and variety of data have put forward higher requirements for the proof and verification of identity information. Achieving decentralized digital identity management helps to improve the performance of relevant proofs and authentication. The Decentralized Identity (DID) system is the link between the real and the virtual, giving physical entities digital identities that enable them to participate in Internet activities. However, faced with the huge number of entities accessing the DID system, the number of DID documents in the system has proliferated. It is still a big challenge to improve the scalability of the system while ensuring the efficiency of information access and verification. In this paper, we propose a blockchain-based verifiable decentralized identity system for cyber-physical web 3.0. First, we propose a blockchain-based system architecture with a specially designed storage structure for DID documents. Specifically, we design a structure based on Merkle Tree that visually summarises the physical associations of entities and reduces access overhead. Second, we design a verification scheme that enables users to verify the integrity of the identity data of the proof provider. We implemented the system framework and conducted experiments to evaluate the performance of our system. The experimental results proved the effectiveness of the system.

articleTitle: Business Process Optimization Analysis of Enterprise E-commerce Logistics Distribution Center
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: With the rapid development of e-commerce, corporate e-commerce logistics and distribution centers are playing an increasingly important role in the national economy. However, some problems in the distribution center business process affect logistics efficiency and customer satisfaction. This article first analyzes the business processes of enterprise e-commerce logistics distribution centers, summarizes some common problems, analyzes the causes of these problems, and proposes a series of optimization strategies. The article includes improving the quality of warehousing space use, adopting a refined management model, effectively organizing distribution route planning, and establishing an information feedback mechanism. Implementing these strategies will help improve logistics efficiency and customer satisfaction, giving enterprises an invincible position in the fierce market competition.

articleTitle: Pre-Hospital Patient Dispatch Optimization Model During a Pandemic
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: A pandemic typically leads to a surge in patients, which strains healthcare resources and can potentially result in social unrest. Therefore, studying patient dispatch during a pandemic to optimize the utilization of available medical resources is crucial. This paper proposes a pre-hospital patient dispatch model designed to minimize travel distance. It categorizes both hospitals and patients into multiple types while modelling the patient admission process for hospitals using queuing theory. Subsequently, a case study based on the COVID-19 cases in Yangpu District, Shanghai during January-February 2020 is conducted to demonstrate the model's practicality and analyse the patient dispatch during the pandemic. The results indicated that severe and mild cases from some communities are treated at the same hospital. This aligns with real-life practices where all infected individuals are often directed to designated hospitals, a critical strategy in pandemic management. Moreover, patients in tertiary hospitals generally experience shorter waiting times compared to those in non-tertiary hospitals. Finally, we put forward some management suggestions for the government during a pandemic based on these findings.

articleTitle: Deviation Propagation Network for Key Quality Factors Identification of Complex Assembly Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: The assembly process of complex products involves many process links, which is a dynamic process with multiple variables and complex coupling. Effective quality control of the assembly process plays an important role in improving the consistency of complex product quality. However, in the actual assembly process, even if the quality of each component meets the design requirements, deviations still gradually accumulate and spread in the process, and it is ultimately difficult to ensure the assembly quality. To effectively identify the key assembly features and the deviation propagation paths in the assembly process, this paper investigates the assembly deviation propagation problem of complex assemblies based on complex network theory. Firstly, based on the measured data, feature surface information, and assembly process, a coupled network model of parts-features is constructed for describing the complex assembly systems by taking assembly parts as nodes and assembly relationships as edges. Then, the node importance indexes of the assembly deviation propagation network are measured to identify the key assembly features, and trace and control the corresponding deviation assembly nodes. Finally, as a typical complex multi-stage process, the diesel engine assembly system is used for validation. Through experimental comparison with actual assembly processes, the results show that this method can effectively model the deviation flow in multi-stage assembly processes, identify key quality factors, and achieve deviation traceability.

articleTitle: Sample Imbalance Motor Fault Diagnosis Based on Ant Lion Optimizer Optimized VMD-CWT-CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: In scenarios with sufficient data volume, fault detection incorporating machine learning algorithms or deep learning methodologies will have better results, but reaching high diagnostic accuracy is difficult under conditions of small sample faults, along with the significant variation in the quantity of samples between normal and fault states. To tackle the problem of data imbalance between normal and fault states, this paper proposes a VMD-CWT -CNN model optimized with the ALO algorithm. Firstly, the VMD is adaptively decomposed using the ALO algorithm, and the IMF components are concatenated to enhance the sample set, thereby increasing the number of fault samples. Secondly, the CWT transformation is applied to create an image dataset. Finally, different datasets are designed to perform fault diagnosis with the CNN. Testing with the suggested approach reveals an average accuracy of 98.3%, effectively addressing the issue of sample imbalance with improved robustness and more accurate diagnostic results.

articleTitle: Robust Decision-Making for Off-Ramp in Intention-Based Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: Deep reinforcement learning has demonstrated its effectiveness in autonomous driving decision-making. The real-world vehicle decision-making process is complex and involves many types of information. Limitations in state information can hinder agents from making optimal decisions, increasing the risk of serious consequences like collisions. We introduce a ro-bust deep reinforcement learning methodology that incorporates driving intention recognition for the decision-making of highway autonomous vehicles during off-ramp scenarios. By using driving intention recognition results, this approach enhances driving safety. A series of experiments utilizing the SUMO and NGSIM US101 datasets support the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed model. Comparative analytical experiments show that the model outperforms other approaches in average return value, average speed, average steps, and success rate. Additionally, the model exhibits consistent success rates under different road traffic density scenarios, highlighting its robustness. The source code is accessible at https://github.com/ColinFanghz/off-ramp-dir-DRL.it.

articleTitle: A Multi-Class Imbalanced Learning Method Using Random Balanced Sampling for Predicting the Quality Level of Diesel Engines
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: Numerous process items and procedures in the assembly process of a diesel engine have a direct and significant impact on its performance, and accurate and effective assembly process control is a key technical bottleneck in improving the quality consistency of batch-produced diesel engines. Accurate prediction of assembly quality can provide support for online control of assembly quality. However, due to the significant class imbalance between qualified and unqualified products of diesel engine assembly quality, the traditional imbalance learning makes it difficult to capture the small changes between classes. Therefore, an improved random balance sampling method is proposed, combined with the LightGBM classifier to create a quality prediction model. Firstly, class balancing of the training dataset is achieved by generating random weights for each class and fusing oversampling and undersampling. Then, a LightGBM-based quality prediction model is built. Finally, the effectiveness of this approach is validated using real industrial diesel engine assembly data. The comparison results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional resampling techniques. This study provides an accurate quality prediction model, laying the groundwork for the assembly quality control model of diesel engines.

articleTitle: A Method for Constructing Engineering-Biology Domain Knowledge Network Oriented Toward Collective Intelligence Innovation Design
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: In the context of the era of information, the growth of personalized user needs and the development of Internet plus technology have brought new challenges and opportunities to product innovation design. As an emerging design mode, collective intelligence design can acquire design knowledge through group wisdom and extensive range to improve the market adaptability of products and the innovation ability of enterprises. As a kind of long-distance knowledge, biology domain knowledge can effectively play the incentive role of cross-domain knowledge in the collective intelligence design process. However, there is currently no effective way of combining engineering with biology domain knowledge to underpin the design process. To address this issue, we propose a method for constructing an engineering-biology domain knowledge network for collective intelligence innovation design: a cross-domain knowledge representation model is constructed to achieve unified representation of engineering and biology domain knowledge; By using cross-domain entity extraction and relationship generation methods, an engineering-biology domain knowledge network is automatically constructed. This method provides a new perspective for cross-domain knowledge motivation and inspiration in collective intelligence innovation design. Through the representation and relationship generation of cross-domain knowledge, our engineering-biology domain knowledge network can provide designers with long-distance design knowledge incentives, improving the quality and innovation of generated solutions.

articleTitle: Dual AGV Formation Control in Automated Ports with Time-Delay Compensation AEKF
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: With the prosperous development of maritime trade, the trend of large containers is becoming more prominent. To effectively solve the compatibility problem between Automated Guided Vehicle(AGV) and containers in ports, dual AGV collaborative handling strategy has received great attention from the industry. However, the time-delay between AGVs during the motion of the dual AGV formation have a significant impact on the control accuracy, stability, and safety. To address the aforementioned pain points, a time-delay compensation method based on an Adaptive Extended Kalman Filter(AEKF) is proposed in this paper, and a Dual-Loop Sliding Mode Controller(DLSMC) is designed for the control of dual AGV formation based on the leader-follower strategy. Finally, the research method is tested and validated in a simulation environment, indicating that the proposed AEKF method can effectively compensate for time-delay and accurately predict the desired trajectory of the follower AGV, which can significantly improve the AGV's speed. Under the action of the DLSMC, the follower AGV can smoothly track the desired trajectory. The error during cured driving can quickly converge, and high-precision parking targets can be achieved at docking point

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Large-Scale Efficient Routing of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: Future smart transportation is anticipated to be much enhanced by autonomous electric vehicles, but efficient routing remains a challenge due to uncertainties and time constraints. Exact solutions for vehicle routing problem (VRP) can not provide a timely solution when the problem size increases. Heuristic and meta-heuristic strategies enhance the exact methods, particularly for mid-sized problems. However, the need for accurate and timely solutions is still an open issue, especially dealing with large-scale VRPs. We propose a novel approach that uses deep reinforcement learning addressing the VRP for electric vehicles with stochastic uncertainties. The problem is mathematically formulated and represented as a Markov Decision Process and a deep Q-Network with custom-designed reward is proposed. The performance of the proposed approach is assessed against Google-OR tools, IBM CPLEX, and state-of-the-art reinforcement learning-based algorithms. The evaluations show that the proposed methods can handle large-scale instances with uncertainties and exceed them in many cases.

articleTitle: Research on the General Development Method of Auto Start-Stop System for Nuclear Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: During startup and shutdown of a pressurized water reactor (PWR) nuclear power plant, it involves a large number of operations on pumps, valves, electric heaters and control rods, and needs to take into account the close coordination of the operating status of each system. At present, the start-stop control is mainly realized by manual operation of the operator, which is very demanding for the operator, and is not only prone to leakage and mis-operation, but even has the risk of causing the unit to deviate from normal operation. Application of advanced automation and intelligent technology to realize automatic start/stop of nuclear power units, which is extremely important in theory and practical significance for the improvement of the operational safety and economics of nuclear power plants. In this paper, PWR nuclear power plant is used as the object of study, analyzes and forms the overall development route of automatic start-stop system for nuclear power plant, and divides into three stages: system R&D and design, logic configuration implementation, system commissioning operation. Then the paper puts forward the specific working methods, principles and step suggestions for each stage of work, so as to lay a solid foundation for the subsequent R&D and application of the automatic start-stop system in nuclear power plants.

articleTitle: Construction Waste Group-buying Trading
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: To address the shortcomings of the current digital trading approach for construction waste recycled products (CWRPs), this paper proposes a combinatorial group-buying auction mechanism. The design of group-buying rule considers both the number of matched buyers and their collective purchasing volume of CWRPs, thus capturing the key characteristic of economies of scale in bulk construction material procurement. Results from numerical experiment suggests that the implementation of the proposed mechanism is more viable and significantly enhances social welfare.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Real-Time Scheduling for Reconfigurable Workshop Using End-to-End Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (ICaMaL)
abstract: The multi-variety and small-batch production mode has made reconfigurable manufacturing systems a promising manufacturing paradigm. Meanwhile, frequent dynamic events in the workshop require scheduling methods with fast response capability. Therefore, this paper proposed a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method for dynamic reconfigurable shop scheduling problem to minimize the total weighted tardiness. Specifically, a real-time scheduling framework is proposed firstly. Then, a DRL-based agent training algorithm is developed, where the state spaces with generality, rule weighting based action spaces, and a reward function based on the estimated weighted tardiness are designed for two agents. Moreover, a mechanism is proposed for handling new job arrivals and job reworks. The experimental results on 120 instances show that the proposed method can obtain better solutions than nine high-quality composite rules, and can effectively deal with dynamic events through training and learning.
